name: The Barrow Roll
description: Sheets of limed calfskin sewn to a bronze ring, the ring green and the skin the colour of tea, taken out of the Bell Cist at Hollin Barrow. It is a roll of the dead the way the Wardens' is a roll of the living, and the last forty lines are in the same hand as the first, which is not possible and is nevertheless the case.

name: The Roll-Warden's Seal
description: A boxwood handle and a disc of brass cut with a bell and a line of five strokes: the mark a Roll-Warden presses under a name to say that a living hand entered it and a living mouth read it aloud. There are three of these and the Wardens want them back.

name: Ondrael's Sand-Glass
description: A quarter-minute glass in a frame of pear-wood, the sand ground from Skerrow limestone because lake sand clumps in the damp. Forty-one years of one woman's held breath have gone through it. She will want it back, and she will not ask for it.

name: The Figures
description: A Tollmere clerk's exercise book gone soft at the corners, ruled into four columns in a hand that has not changed since the sixth page. It is a measurement nobody has published and the only copy, and its owner has twice been asked why not and twice given the honest answer.

name: Tessane's Lantern
description: An Isseva burial lantern of indigo paper on an alder frame, relit every year for ninety-odd years by a family who could not have told you whose it was. A reed stands uncut in the oil-well, which in the marsh means a drowned person nobody could bury, and Tessane did not drown.
